source: Float sample monitoring data + Dr. Walker entry-form batch 2 (reviewed, confirmed 2026-06-23)
notes: Ground-truth labels for the monitoring-extraction loop. Each element of `situations` is one parent monitoring entry (occurrence); a recurring situation appears as multiple elements sharing a name. `fear_rating` is the parent's own number or null (never estimated). `behaviors` is ordered; one entry can hold a sequence (e.g. avoidance -> escape). `decision_ref` points to the entry in Float-Extraction-Decisions-Log.md that drove a non-obvious label. | fear_rating_max is optional, present only for a genuine same-trigger range (one trigger whose intensity varies by occurrence). diagnosis is case-level metadata; the behavior taxonomy is diagnosis-agnostic. in_session_questions (parent/patient) seed the Stage 2 templates.

definitions.avoidance: Child does not enter the situation.
definitions.escape: Child was already in the situation and leaves once anxiety spikes.
definitions.safety: Child stays in the situation but acts to feel safer or reduce attention (incl. reassurance-seeking, keeping a parent close).
definitions.unclear: Note doesn't give enough detail to classify; flag rather than guess.

rules.R1: fear_rating is the parent's own number or null; never estimated.
rules.R3: OCD / ritual / compulsion presentations out of scope for now.

taxonomy.diagnosis_field: Descriptive metadata only. NOT consumed by extraction or question generation. The diagnostic pattern is implicit in the inputs; the pipeline keys off extracted triggers, behaviors, and accommodations, never the diagnosis label. Recording it would let the model shortcut into clinical authority, which is out of scope.
taxonomy.stage_2_questions: in_session_questions are generated from the extracted pattern (mix of triggers, behavior types, accommodations), not from the diagnosis. Parent- and patient-facing sets are distinct outputs.

accommodations.description: Parent emails the teacher to arrange a lunch buddy

behaviors.description: Wears headphones so nobody talks to her

cases.source_note: (Lunchtime at school, fear 8/10) Mia ate in the library again instead of the cafeteria. She said the cafeteria was too loud but then admitted she didn't want to sit alone. Parent did: I emailed her teacher to ask about a lunch buddy. (Lunchtime at school, fear 6/10) She went to the cafeteria but wore her headphones the whole time so nobody would talk to her. Parent did: I told her that was a good first step.

cases.title: Health worries

behaviors.description: Stops the activity and comes inside when he notices body sensations
Repeatedly asks whether his heart is OK (reassurance-seeking)

accommodations.description: Parent checks his pulse and repeatedly reassures him

behaviors.description: Refuses to go to school when he feels unwell
Asks to see a doctor to check he is not seriously ill

accommodations.description: Parent keeps him home from school when he reports feeling unwell
Parent books doctor's appointments in response to his health worries

cases.source_note: (Noticing body sensations after activity, fear 7/10) After running around in the yard Theo noticed his heart beating fast. He stopped playing and came inside, then kept asking me if his heart was OK and whether he needed to see a doctor. Parent did: I checked his pulse, told him he was fine, and reassured him several times. (Feeling unwell before school, fear 8/10) Theo said his stomach felt strange and he was sure something was wrong. He didn't want to go to school and asked to see a doctor. Parent did: I kept him home and booked a doctor's appointment to put his mind at rest.

cases.title: Separation from parent at home

situations.name: At home when parent is not in the same room

behaviors.description: Calls out to parent, stays by her side, repeatedly asks about her location (reassurance-seeking)
Refuses sitters

accommodations.description: Parent allows the child to stay with her
Parent doesn't go out unless she must
Parent never goes out unless the father is home

parent: What do you worry will happen if you leave him with a sitter or his father?
patient: What do you worry will happen if your mom is not with you?

cases.source_note: (At home when M, age 6, and I are not in the same room, fear 8/10) M cries, pleads, hyperventilates, and gets so upset he almost vomits when I have to be out of the house without him for even an hour. He calls out to me, stays by my side, and asks many questions about where I am throughout the day. He refuses sitters. Parent did: I avoid leaving him; I don't go out unless I must, and never unless his father is home.

accommodations.description: Parents provide excessive reassurance before and during the absence

parent: What are you concerned will happen to F if you do not text with her or reassure her?
What is your theory about what Francis fears will happen when you are away?

behaviors.description: Asks many questions about party location and timing, texts and calls nonstop telling them to come home (reassurance-seeking)

accommodations.description: Parents provide excessive reassurance before and during the absence

cases.source_note: (Parent out at dinner, fear 7/10) F begs us not to go, sometimes says she feels sick, asks all sorts of questions about where the restaurant is and who we're going with, and texts and calls us after we've been away thirty minutes. Parent did: We reassure her she'll be fine, make sure our long-time sitter comes, give her text updates that all is well, and tell her we'll come home early -- and we do come home before we want to. (Parent out at a party, fear 9/10) F asks lots of questions about the party location, how long we'll stay, and when we'll be back, then texts and calls nonstop telling us to come home and asking where we are. Parent did: We give the same reassurance before and during.
